second_order: Carrying on ordinary arguments and jokes inside selected threads
theme_note: These passages continue the thread's own dispute, joke, correction, or aside while the selected April Fools conduct occurs around them; what holds them together is continuing ordinary conversation, not shared vocabulary.

second_order: Enforcing and performing no swearsies wholesomeness
theme_note: Moderator-operated replies and participants impose, repeat, obey, parody, or test the room's wholesome and no-swearsies rule.

second_order: Pushing back on the wholesome takeover and moderator control
theme_note: Participants curse, evade, test, mock, or demand an end to the wholesome rules, restricted posting, and moderator-led joke.

second_order: Calling out normies and bad meme sources
theme_note: Participants guard the dank/normie boundary by rejecting posts, watermarks, sources, reposts, and styles they call normie or cancer.
Posters and commenters deliberately enact the room's temporary normie register through stale catchphrases, emoji, exaggerated praise, and mocked meme sources.

second_order: Working out the April Fools bamboozle
theme_note: Participants identify the calendar joke, explain confusing posts and rules as April Fools, or revise an earlier reading after recognising the prank.

second_order: Applying ordinary submission and meme-quality rules amid the jokes
theme_note: Community-operated moderation applies account-history, link-format, caption, voting, repost, and dankness rules without adopting the proposal it answers.

second_order: Joining the Wholesome Network and naming its friends
theme_note: Moderator announcements make the room and named neighbouring subreddits members or friends of the Wholesome Network.

second_order: Answering with Data for one day
theme_note: Participants answer confusion with Data, recall the vanished routine, and later explain that every comment had to be Data for one day.

second_order: Throwing one-off ideas and sightings at r/place
theme_note: These passages point to a drawing, ask for a pixel or image, or offer an isolated canvas idea without establishing a shared ongoing project.

second_order: Raiding and taking spots on the canvas
theme_note: Participants call for deleting, overwriting, invading, or taking named canvas areas and sometimes supply targets or assent.

second_order: Showing people where and how to use r/place
theme_note: Participants ask what or where a canvas target is, give directions or coordinates, explain the pixel timer, and acknowledge the help.

second_order: Calling for the Redankening after April Fools
theme_note: Participants say April Fools is over, call for dank memes again, name the Redankening, and argue over whether the room has returned.

second_order: Raiding one Instagram normie after the fiasco
theme_note: A post-April-Fools call names a target, recruits raiders, elicits action reports and direct-message accounts, and draws objections and an abort call.

second_order: Building named drawings from coordinates and help calls
theme_note: Calls name a drawing or message, anchor it with coordinates, recruit helpers, accept the work, or move its coordination to Discord.

second_order: Reporting, mourning, and sharing what happened on the canvas
theme_note: Participants point out completed drawings, report deletion or failure, say it is too late, mourn the closed canvas, credit creation, or share a timelapse.

second_order: Blaming moderator-only posting for an iFunny trip
theme_note: Participants recount going back to iFunny because only moderators could post here, then argue over what the caption means and who is normie.
